definitions.explanation: Paper specifically designed for writing letters, typically with lines or decorative borders. A staple item in Japanese stationery culture.

examples.japanese: {便箋|びんせん}に{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a letter on writing paper.

examples.japanese: {花柄|はながら}の{便箋|びんせん}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought letter paper with a floral pattern.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}に{感謝|かんしゃ}の{気持|きも}ちを{込|こ}めて、きれいな{便箋|びんせん}で{手紙|てがみ}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a letter to my grandmother on beautiful stationery to express my gratitude.

notes:
Japan has a rich stationery culture, and {便箋|びんせん} comes in many designs, from simple lined paper to elaborate seasonal patterns. Often sold as a set together with {封筒|ふうとう} (envelopes). Handwritten letters on nice {便箋|びんせん} are considered more heartfelt than typed or digital messages.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{便箋|びんせん}と{封筒|ふうとう} (letter paper and envelopes)
・{便箋|びんせん}セット (stationery set)
・{罫線|けいせん}{入|い}りの{便箋|びんせん} (lined letter paper)
